Approximate log-likelihood and DIC (experimental)

Source: R/loglik.R
psp_loglik.Rd

The likelihood of a spatial probit model is an \(NT\)-dimensional normal rectangle probability with no closed form. psp_loglik() estimates it with the GHK simulator (Geweke, Hajivassiliou and Keane), applied to the sparse precision matrix of the latent outcomes so that it scales to large \(N\). For random-effects models the random effects are added to the latent vector and integrated out with it (type = "marginal"), or held at their posterior draws (type = "conditional").

Usage

psp_loglik(
  fit,
  draws = 100,
  reps = 200,
  type = c("marginal", "conditional"),
  seed = 1
)

# S3 method for class 'psprobit'
logLik(object, reps = 500, seed = 1, ...)

psp_dic(fit, draws = 100, reps = 200, seed = 1)

Arguments

fit, object

A fitted psprobit object.

draws

Number of posterior draws to evaluate.

reps

Number of GHK replications per evaluation.

type

"marginal" (random effects integrated out) or "conditional" (given the random-effect draws kept by the sampler). The two coincide for pooled models.

seed

Seed for the GHK replications (the same random numbers are used for every draw).

...

Unused.

Value

psp_loglik(): a vector of log-likelihood values, one per draw, with attribute mcse. logLik(): a logLik object. psp_dic(): a list with dic, p_d (effective number of parameters), d_bar (posterior mean deviance) and d_hat (deviance at the posterior mean).

Details

The GHK estimate of the likelihood is unbiased, but its logarithm is biased downwards when the replications vary a lot; increase reps until the estimates settle, and compare models with the same reps and seed (common random numbers). attr(, "mcse") gives a delta-method Monte Carlo standard error for each value, and a warning is given when it exceeds 0.5. Without random effects to integrate out (pooled models, or type = "conditional") the periods are independent and are simulated separately, which keeps the error small even for large panels. The marginal likelihood of a random-effects model is a single \(NT\)-dimensional problem and becomes unreliable beyond a few hundred observations.

logLik() evaluates the marginal log-likelihood at the posterior mean of the parameters, so AIC() and BIC() work. psp_dic() computes the deviance information criterion (Spiegelhalter et al. 2002) from the marginal likelihood.

The posterior draws are processed in parallel under the user's future::plan() (see "Parallel post-processing" in psp_control()).

References

Geweke, J. (1991). Efficient simulation from the multivariate normal and Student-t distributions subject to linear constraints. Computer Science and Statistics: Proceedings of the 23rd Symposium on the Interface, 571-578.

Spiegelhalter, D. J., Best, N. G., Carlin, B. P. and van der Linde, A. (2002). Bayesian measures of model complexity and fit. JRSS B 64, 583-639.

Examples

W <- psp_weights(rook_weights(4, 4), style = "W")
d <- sim_psprobit(W, T = 3, beta = c(0, 1), rho = 0.4, seed = 2)
fit <- psprobit(y ~ x1, data = d, index = c("id", "time"), W = W, impacts = FALSE,
                control = psp_control(iter = 200, warmup = 100, chains = 1, seed = 2))
#> Warning: Possible convergence problems (R-hat > 1.01 or bulk ESS < 100) for: (Intercept), x1, rho, sigma_alpha. Consider more iterations.
logLik(fit, reps = 200)
#> Warning: The GHK estimates are unreliable (Monte Carlo se up to 0.94 on the log scale): increase 'reps'. GHK needs many replications for large N x T.
#> 'log Lik.' -36.6207 (df=4)
psp_dic(fit, draws = 20, reps = 100)
#> Warning: The GHK estimates are unreliable (Monte Carlo se up to 1.00 on the log scale): increase 'reps'. GHK needs many replications for large N x T.
#> Warning: Negative p_D: the GHK error dominates; increase 'reps'.
#> $dic
#> [1] 53.78186
#> 
#> $p_d
#> [1] -18.66173
#> 
#> $d_bar
#> [1] 72.44359
#> 
#> $d_hat
#> [1] 91.10532
#>
